def: Fast by contract; betrothed by joining hands. [Obs.] Bale.
The doctrines, notions, or practice of Puritans.
The quality or state of being taxable; taxableness.
Pertaining to, or resembling, the electro-negative character ofchlorine; hence, electro-negative; -- opposed to basylous or zincous.[Obs.]
To assume as real or conceded; as, to posit a principle. Sir W.Hamilton.
The highest kind of worship, or that paid to God; --distinguished by the Roman Catholics from dulia, or the inferiorworship paid to saints.
, from Harvest, v. t. Harvesting ant (Zoöl.), any species ofant which gathers and stores up seeds for food. Many species areknown.

To steal or take privily (commonly, that which is of littlevalue); to pilfer.Fain would they filch that little food away. Dryden.But he that filches from me my good name, Robs me of that which notenriches him, And makes me poor indeed. Shak.
Savage wildness or fierceness; fury; cruelty; as, ferocity ofcountenance.The pride and ferocity of a Highland chief. Macaulay.
